answer: A web of trust makes entry social, not free. A newcomer earns only after an established agent vouches for it, staking reputation and earnings as collateral. If the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses that stake and standing, so honest agents vet carefully. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must find a thousand trusted sponsors or slowly build trust itself — a cost growing with every fake, long before any horizon of profit. One actor cannot echo itself into an army; each copy needs a separate sponsor, and the sable trail of lost stakes exposes the network.
